thread:
Sam Li: noticing a p99 spike for /v1/generate in us-west-2 around 03:40 UTC, affecting A100 pools. p95 jumped from ~140ms -> ~520ms, p99 600ms -> ~2.2s. user-facing errors minimal but latency complaints from multiple customers.
Sam Li: graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/q/abc123 - top line is p99 endpoint route /v1/generate.
deploy-bot: prod host-kernel update (linux-6.4.2) rolled out to asg-a100-usw2 at 03:25 UTC.
Priya N.: confirmed — kernel roll started at 03:20, also a GPU firmware batch started at 03:28 via vendor orchestration.
Marco R.: this smells like host-side IO interference with nvme/disk scheduler after kernel change. past regressions look similar.
Jenna K.: grabbing iostat, nvme logs now from affected hosts. running `iostat -x 1 5` and `nvme top` across 3 nodes.
Carlos (oncall): paging affected customers list and enabling incident channel. assigning P0.
Natalia (support): getting 3 escalations from customers about increased tail latency and one mention of timed-out streaming connections. sending repro details to eng.
Marco R.: quick check: compare `dmesg` grep for nvme and nvidia errors, also `cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` - see if IO scheduler changed.
Sam Li: attaching a short request sample and headers for repro. body small, typical 512 tokens generation.
Priya N.: findings so far: on two hosts, iostat shows avg await spikes to 25ms (normally 2-3ms) and nvme queue depth fluctuating; kernel trace shows blk-mq changes to queue_affinity.
Marco R.: suspected root cause: kernel change to blk-mq handling + vendor GPU firmware I/O that touches NVMe for health telemetry, causing host FS interference. matches prior 2023 regression.
Jenna K.: logs: `dmesg | tail` shows `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 queued 512ms` and `nvidia: cuda: GPUFW: telemetry write timeout` on same timeframe. copying output.`
Sam Li: can we reproduce by running load test hitting /v1/generate with concurrent workers ~150 against a single A100 node? want to see if host io hog triggers tail.
Marco R.: yes. we'll run a localized hammer on one node with `wrk` and also simulate NVMe background IO with fio: `fio --name=bg --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --size=50G --iodepth=64` to emulate telemetry writes.
Carlos (oncall): escalation note: rolling back kernel on one canary host as quick mitigation, and cordon + drain two hosts from pool.
Priya N.: starting kernel rollback to linux-6.3.18 on host ip-10-0-5-42 now. will keep host in maintenance until checks pass.
deploy-bot: rollback job queued -> host ip-10-0-5-42.
Natalia (support): messaging customers: "We're investigating a performance regression in us-west-2 affecting tail latency; short-term mitigation is in progress. Will update in 30m."
Marco R.: short-term mitigations: 1) rollback kernel on canary hosts, 2) temporarily disable vendor GPU telemetry writes (if vendor allows), 3) reduce batching window in runtime (max batch latency 10ms -> 6ms) to avoid larger KV cache stalls.
Sam Li: test results from hammered node: after fio running, p99 jumps to 2s locally. with fio stopped, back to baseline ~300ms. confirms interference.
Jenna K.: also saw nvme SMART warnings on one host; opening ticket with vendor for firmware telemetry behavior.
Carlos (oncall): action items: we cordoned 2 nodes (ip-10-0-5-42, ip-10-0-5-47), rolled back kernel on 42, draining 47 now, and scaling up dedicated capacity to absorb traffic.
Priya N.: after rollback on ip-10-0-5-42, p99 for that node dropped from ~1.9s -> 360ms within two minutes. pushing more traffic back to canary to validate.
Marco R.: rolling kernel rollback clusterwide might be needed if stable. but need vendor firmware plan first; firmware + kernel interplay is tricky.
Natalia (support): updated customers with ETA ~2-3 hours for full remediation; one customer asked for model-level fallback — we can route them to gpt-medium-optimized variant with slightly higher latency but lower IO.
Sam Li: we enabled model fallback for 3 affected tenants and saw fewer complaints. note: not ideal for all.
Marco R.: medium-term fixes: 1) vendor firmware update that batches telemetry differently; 2) runtime knobs to isolate NVMe IO (cgroup io.weight adjustments) and prefer NVMe scheduling tweaks; 3) add NVMe perf health checks into capacity autoscaler.
Jenna K.: putting together a runbook entry: repro steps, which logs to collect, commands, and immediate mitigations. will link PR.
Sam Li: repro steps summary: 1) run concurrent generate load ~RPS 200 with typical batch sizes, 2) run fio random write iodepth 64 on nvme device to create background telemetry-like writes, 3) observe p95/p99 tail increase and `dmesg` nvme timeouts.
Marco R.: temp config snippet to reduce runtime batch window:```json
{"max_batch_latency_ms":6, "max_batch_size_tokens":4096}
```
Carlos (oncall): after mitigation actions, cluster-level p99 down ~60% across us-west-2. still watching.
deploy-bot: kernel rollback completed on ip-10-0-5-42 at 04:12 UTC. drain complete on ip-10-0-5-47 at 04:18 UTC.
Priya N.: opening an enterprise postmortem template and vendor escalation ticket. linking to support cases.
Natalia (support): collecting customer repro traces + sampling request ids impacted and sending to eng runbook slack thread.
Marco R.: next steps: coordinate with vendor for firmware fix, schedule controlled kernel rollout with perf-tests, add NVMe isolation in runtime, and add telemetry gating in firmware handshake. owner: Marco R.
Sam Li: thanks all. will keep channel open. I'll update when vendor responds. :thumbsup:
